StarRocks is an open-source SQL engine for analytics. You can use it to
query data from a Shiny dashboard with each visitor's database permissions.

`oauth_db_starrocks()` opens a DBI connection using the visitor's signed
access token. StarRocks verifies the token and applies the database user's
privileges. Your app can then use SQL or dbplyr to read the data.

## Try the local demo

With Docker running, `shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("starrocks")` starts a
configured server, Keycloak sign-in and an app with Alice and Bob's accounts.
Docker supplies the database driver too. See
[Getting started](getting-started.html#build-a-small-app) for credentials
and cleanup. The StarRocks images use amd64 and need about 4 GB of Docker
memory.

## Values for your own server

Install
[MySQL Connector/ODBC](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/connector-odbc/en/connector-odbc-installation.html)
9.2 or later with its OpenID Connect plugin. Your StarRocks 3.5+ server must accept JWT access tokens; the detailed
server setup follows the app.

| Setting | Where to get it |
| --- | --- |
| `OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_SERVER` | The cluster's MySQL endpoint hostname; the default port is 9030 |
| `database` | The StarRocks database your users can query |
| `OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_DRIVER` | The registered driver name from `odbc::odbcListDrivers()` |
| `OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_SSL_CA` | The CA certificate for that endpoint |
| Issuer, client ID, secret | Your [OIDC app registration](getting-started.html#register-your-app) |

Save the `OAUTHDB_*` values in `.Renviron` and restart R. The app requests
the database username from the login; configure the matching principal
claim on StarRocks.

## Complete Shiny app

Register your app with the trusted identity provider and configure its
audience and scopes for StarRocks. Use `http://localhost:8100` as the local
redirect URI. Set `OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_ISSUER`, `OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_SERVER`,
`OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_DRIVER`, `OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_SSL_CA`, `OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID`,
and `OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET` in your environment. The example uses the
validated ID token's preferred username; select the claim your server maps.

After signing in,
click **Load rows**. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

```{r app, eval=FALSE}
pkgs <- c("shiny", "shinyOAuth", "shinyOAuthDB", "mirai", "odbc")
for (pkg in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_ISSUER")
)

client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "email", "offline_access")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())
  con <- oauth_db_starrocks(
    auth$connection,
    server = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_SERVER"),
    database = "reporting",
    user = function() {
      reference <- req(auth$connection())
      identity <- reference$identity(claims = "preferred_username")
      req(identity$id_token_claims$preferred_username)
    },
    driver = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_DRIVER"),
    ssl_ca = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_STARROCKS_SSL_CA")
  )
  query_task <- oauth_db_task(con)
  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke("SELECT CURRENT_USER() AS database_user")
  })
  output$rows <- renderTable(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*", onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)
    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.
```

Save this as `example.R`, replace the database and claim mapping, and run
`source("example.R")`. Use `target` when your shinyOAuth client
contains named token targets. No separate browser authentication is
performed by the database driver.

## Configure server authentication and the driver

Use StarRocks 3.5 or later with JWT authentication. Configure a trusted
JWKS, the exact issuer and audience, and a principal claim that maps to
the StarRocks username. Grant the user or group its database privileges.
See [JWT authentication](https://docs.starrocks.io/docs/administration/user_privs/authentication/jwt_authentication/)
and [security integrations](https://docs.starrocks.io/docs/administration/user_privs/authentication/security_integration/).

Install the R package `odbc` and MySQL Connector/ODBC 9.2 or later, including
its `authentication_openid_connect_client` plugin. A MariaDB driver or an
older MySQL driver is not sufficient. List installed driver names with
`odbc::odbcListDrivers()` and pass the registered name as `driver`.
On Unix, a driver library path may also be accepted by the driver manager.
Windows requires the driver to be installed and registered.
Set `plugin_dir` if the driver cannot find its installed authentication
plugins. See MySQL's [authentication options](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/connector-odbc/en/connector-odbc-configuration-authentication.html).

Enable TLS for the StarRocks MySQL endpoint. The helper requires server
identity verification; supply `ssl_ca` for a private CA. Use the hostname
in the server certificate. The default query port is 9030.

The helper uses the visitor's **access token** from shinyOAuth. Configure
the provider and StarRocks to accept that JWT with its issuer, audience,
and principal claim. A provider that issues only opaque access tokens,
or an integration that accepts only that provider's ID tokens, needs a
different provider configuration before using this helper.

## Connection lifetime and queries

Get a current connection inside each render or reactive expression:

```{r queries, eval=FALSE}
connection <- con()
DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT id, total FROM orders LIMIT 20")
dplyr::tbl(connection, "orders") |>
  dplyr::filter(total >= 100) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

The helper keeps a valid SQL connection through token renewal and replaces
it when the account or username changes. Sign-out and session end close
the connection. If it breaks, call `con()` to reopen it; the helper doesn't
replay failed queries. See `?oauth_db_starrocks` for driver and connection
options.
